tweaks.name: Background game recording
tweaks.explanation: The Xbox Game Bar records your matches continuously, even when you never asked it to.
tweaks.consequence: You lose the automatic replay of the last few minutes of play (Win+Alt+G).

tweaks.name: Windows Game Mode
tweaks.explanation: Windows reserves resources for the foreground game and defers background work such as driver installation.
tweaks.consequence: None. The rare regressions on record date back to early Windows 10 builds.
tweaks.gain: small but never negative on Windows 11

tweaks.name: Foreground application priority
tweaks.explanation: Gives the active window more processor time at the expense of the background. This is the setting other tools call “system profile” without ever saying what it does.
tweaks.consequence: Background work — compiling, encoding, downloading — gets somewhat slower while you play.
tweaks.gain: check it on the benchmark: measurable, but not reliably positive

tweaks.name: Background Store apps
tweaks.explanation: Stops Microsoft Store apps from running while they are not in the foreground. Does not affect Chrome, Discord, or any ordinary program.
tweaks.consequence: No more background notifications or syncing for those apps: Mail, Calendar, Photos.
tweaks.gain: none at all if you don't use Store apps

tweaks.name: Firmware-injected programs (WPBT)
tweaks.explanation: The Windows Platform Binary Table lets your motherboard have Windows run a program at every boot. It is the mechanism some vendors use to reinstall their software even after a clean format.
tweaks.consequence: None on a self-built PC. On a branded machine, a vendor utility may stop reinstalling itself — usually the whole point.
tweaks.gain: no performance gain — hygiene and control over your machine

tweaks.name: Virtualization-based security (VBS)
tweaks.explanation: Windows runs permanently under a hypervisor. This only earns its cost if a service actually uses it — Credential Guard, Memory Integrity, Hyper-V, WSL, Docker or Windows Sandbox.
tweaks.consequence: Put it back before installing WSL, Docker or Windows Sandbox. Windows may re-enable it after a major version update.
tweaks.gain: a few percent — far less than Memory Integrity costs

tweaks.name: Xbox Game Bar
tweaks.explanation: The overlay that opens with Win+G stays loaded while you play.
tweaks.consequence: Win+G no longer opens anything. Screenshots go through another tool.
tweaks.gain: a few tenths of a percent

tweaks.name: Multi-plane overlay (MPO)
tweaks.explanation: Windows composes the image from several hardware layers. On many configurations this causes micro-stutter in borderless fullscreen.
tweaks.consequence: Slightly higher idle GPU power draw. Requires a restart.

tweaks.name: Mouse acceleration
tweaks.explanation: Windows amplifies your fast movements, which makes aim impossible to reproduce from one flick to the next.
tweaks.consequence: The desktop pointer feels slower at first. That is the intended behaviour in game.

tweaks.name: Peer-to-peer sharing of Windows updates
tweaks.explanation: Your PC uploads Windows updates to other PCs over the internet. This is the single heaviest thing on your ping during a match.
tweaks.consequence: Updates download from Microsoft only, sometimes a little more slowly.
tweaks.gain: latency: several ms of ping saved

tweaks.name: Windows telemetry
tweaks.explanation: Reduces usage-data collection to the minimum your edition of Windows allows.

tweaks.name: Advertising ID
tweaks.explanation: Stops apps from using a unique identifier to target you.

tweaks.name: Bing in Start menu search
tweaks.explanation: Local search also queries the internet, which slows it down and clutters it with web results.

tweaks.name: Silent app reinstallation
tweaks.explanation: Windows quietly reinstalls promotional apps after updates. This is what brings back the things you just uninstalled.
tweaks.consequence: None, beyond the absence of suggestions in the Start menu.
tweaks.gain: no in-game gain — stops removed apps from coming back
